issues.legal_issue: A tenant who erects a building in breach of an unregistered covenant not to build remains entitled to statutory compensation and to seek a sale of the land in a pending ejectment suit.
material_facts: The tenants rented vacant land and continued in possession after the lease term expired.
The written lease prohibited construction, but it was not registered.
The tenants erected buildings on the land in breach of the covenant.
An ejectment suit was pending when the protective legislation became applicable to the area, and the tenants applied for a sale of the land within the prescribed time.
issues.conclusion: The covenant did not defeat the tenants’ entitlement to compensation or their right to seek a sale of the land; the appeal was allowed and the order recognizing their purchase claim was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(4) and 3 of the Madras City Tenants’ Protection Act, 1921, ‘tenant’ includes tenants within the Act’s definition, and the unqualified entitlement to compensation is not limited to buildings erected with the landlord’s permission. Section 9 permits a tenant entitled to compensation to seek a sale of the land in an ejectment suit, and section 10 applies that right to pending suits. Under section 12, a contract cannot take away or limit rights under the Act; its proviso preserves relevant building stipulations only when they are in writing and registered. The court distinguished N. Vajrapani Naidu v. New Theatre Carnatic Talkies Ltd. because it concerned the proviso to section 12, which did not apply here.

rule.if: tenant_of_rented_land and tenant_built_structure and covenant_prohibited_building and covenant_unregistered and protective_law_applies and pending_ejectment_suit and timely_application_for_land_purchase

predicates.tenant_of_rented_land: The person held land as a tenant liable to pay rent for it.
predicates.tenant_built_structure: The tenant erected a structure on the rented land.
predicates.covenant_prohibited_building: The lease included a covenant prohibiting the tenant from building on the land.
predicates.covenant_unregistered: The written covenant was not registered.
predicates.protective_law_applies: The protective law applied to the area where the rented land was situated.
predicates.pending_ejectment_suit: An ejectment suit against the tenant was pending when the tenant sought relief.
predicates.timely_application_for_land_purchase: The tenant applied for the land-purchase remedy within the applicable time limit.

issues.definition: When a tenant of rented land builds a structure despite an unregistered covenant prohibiting construction, and the protective law applies during a pending ejectment suit in which the tenant timely applies to purchase the land, the tenant is entitled to compensation and to seek the purchase.

issues.legal_issue: A preamble describing a narrower legislative purpose cannot restrict clear operative provisions that grant rights without that limitation.
material_facts: The operative provisions granted compensation for a building erected by a tenant without qualifying the building by reference to the tenant’s purpose or expectation when building.
The preamble described protection for tenants who had built in the hope that they would not be evicted.
The landlord relied on the covenant and the preamble to argue that the statutory rights did not extend to the tenants’ buildings.
issues.conclusion: The preamble could not narrow the clear language of the operative provisions or annul the rights those provisions granted.
issues.legal_principle: Clear and unambiguous operative provisions control over a narrower description of purpose in the preamble; a preamble cannot annul an enacted section. The court referred to Maxwell on Interpretation of Statutes, 11th edition, page 45, and Deo v. Brandling (1828), 7 B. & C. 643, 660.

predicates.statutory_benefit_dispute: A dispute concerns whether a person qualifies for a benefit granted by legislation.
predicates.operative_text_covers_buildings_without_: The operative text grants the benefit for buildings without limiting them by the builder’s purpose or expectation.
predicates.preamble_describes_narrower_class: The preamble describes a class narrower than the class covered by the operative text.

issues.definition: When a statutory-benefit dispute involves operative text covering buildings without qualification and a preamble describing a narrower class, the preamble cannot narrow the operative text.
